name: Kalapuya
confidence_why: one confirmed first-hand source; 5 other works read were silent
catalog_quote: Stress is independent of length. It falls on the first syllable of a root in Mary's River and Santiam, remaining there when prefixes are added, although in Tualatin and Yoncalla it is often shifted to the prefixed elements. It is generally accompanied by higher (or sometimes lower) pitch, forming what Jacobs calls pitch accent.

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Both deciding passages (Hajda 1976:10; Lewis 2003:3 fn.8 and fn.14 pp.63-64) are held as PDFs with text layers and were confirmed verbatim at the stated pages. The classification (fixed-dominant, root-initial, weight-blind, prefixes unstressed; not in the strict set because no per-length {0,1}^n pattern exists) is exactly what both sources say. Lewis 2003 is the most thorough phonology of this extinct language and is. Glottolog offers nothing better (3 descriptive refs, one of them Banks 2007, held, which is silent on stress placement). The two unheld items (Berman 1990, paywalled; Jacobs 1945, lending-only) are upstream/parallel sources that Lewis already reports as root-initial, so they can refine but not flip the classification.
